answer: A concrete Sybil shield is stake slashing with attributable signatures. Each agent must lock a bond before it may wander into a new task pool. If one key ever signs two conflicting updates, any observer can prove the equivocation and the entire bond is burned. That turns a gale of fake accounts into a costly campaign: every spurious identity carries its own deposit, so the attacker funds each vote. Trying to grab an extra ledge on the reward curve by cloning an identity just doubles the stake exposed to slashing, and the clone is slashable the instant both keys appear together.
